front: In DynamoDB, the maximum size of one item, attribute names included, is {{c1::400 KB}}.
extra: Attribute names count toward the item size, not only the values.

front: In DynamoDB, one partition serves at most {{c1::3,000 read units per second}} and 1,000 write units per second.
extra: A hot key hits this partition ceiling even when the table has spare capacity.

front: In DynamoDB, the item size of a read is rounded up to the {{c1::next 4 KB multiple}}.
extra: A small item still costs one full read unit.

front: In DynamoDB, the item size of a write is rounded up to the {{c1::next 1 KB multiple}}.
extra: A small item still costs one full write unit.

front: In DynamoDB, the result set of one Query is limited to {{c1::1 MB per call}}.
extra: Read more results with LastEvaluatedKey from the response.

front: In DynamoDB Streams, stream records have a {{c1::lifetime of 24 hours}}.
extra: After that, DynamoDB removes them from the stream automatically.

front: In DynamoDB, one table can have {{c1::up to 5 local secondary indexes}}.
extra: You define them when you create the table.

front: In a DynamoDB table with a local secondary index, one item collection can hold at most {{c1::10 GB}}.
extra: The collection lives in one partition; use a GSI when it can grow larger.

front: In DynamoDB, which read is the default: eventually consistent or strongly consistent?
back: Eventually consistent.
extra: Ask for a strongly consistent read when the read must see the latest write.

front: In DynamoDB, a new app's traffic is unknown and spiky. Which capacity mode fits?
back: On-demand mode: it follows fluctuating traffic without a forecast.
extra: Auto scaling on a provisioned table tends to over-provision or under-provision spiky traffic.

front: In DynamoDB, can a query on a global secondary index be strongly consistent?
back: No. GSI queries support eventual consistency only.
extra: A query on a local secondary index can be strongly consistent.

front: In DynamoDB, does a filter expression lower the read capacity that a Scan consumes?
back: No. The filter runs after the Scan reads the items.
extra: The Scan consumes the same amount of read capacity with or without a filter.

front: In DynamoDB, two items in two tables must change together or not at all. Which API?
back: TransactWriteItems, for an all-or-nothing result.
extra: It works within one table and across tables.

front: In a DynamoDB global table, does a Region outage need a database failover?
back: No. A global table has no primary Region.
extra: The application reads and writes a replica table in a healthy Region.

front: In DynamoDB, can you add a local secondary index to an existing table?
back: No. Add a global secondary index instead.
extra: A local secondary index is created with the table and cannot be deleted later.

front: DynamoDB Streams or Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB: which keeps change records up to 1 year?
back: Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB.
extra: DynamoDB Streams keeps them for 24 hours.

front: In DynamoDB, does time to live (TTL) delete an item at the moment it expires?
back: No. Within a few days of their expiration time.
extra: TTL deletes consume no write throughput.

front: In DAX, does the cache store the results of strongly consistent reads?
back: No. DAX passes them to DynamoDB without caching.
extra: DAX cannot serve a strongly consistent read by itself.

front: In DynamoDB, can a restore overwrite the existing table?
back: No. A restore creates a new table.
extra: Point the application at the restored table, or copy data back.

front: In DynamoDB on-demand mode, does a table absorb any traffic spike at once?
back: No. Instantly, up to double the previous peak.
extra: For a bigger launch, pre-warm the table by raising its warm throughput.

front: In DynamoDB provisioned mode, does auto scaling prevent throttling in a sudden spike?
back: No. Auto scaling does not respond instantly.
extra: It is also limited by the maximum capacity you configure.

front: In DynamoDB, one partition key value gets most writes and is throttled. What do you change?
back: The key: add a random suffix to spread the writes.
extra: Write sharding spreads the writes across a larger key space.

front: In DynamoDB, repeated reads need microsecond latency with minimal code change. What do you add?
back: DAX, the API-compatible in-memory cache for DynamoDB.
extra: DAX serves eventually consistent reads with microsecond latency.

front: DAX or ElastiCache: which one supports data structures such as lists, sets and hashes?
back: ElastiCache.
extra: AWS names ElastiCache as the choice for queries beyond key-value access.

front: In DynamoDB, instances in private subnets must reach a table without a NAT device. What do you add?
back: A gateway endpoint for DynamoDB.
extra: The VPC then needs no internet gateway or NAT device for DynamoDB.

front: In DynamoDB, which endpoint lets on-premises servers reach a table privately: gateway or interface?
back: An interface endpoint, through AWS PrivateLink.
extra: A gateway endpoint does not allow access from on-premises networks.

front: In DynamoDB, storage is most of a table's bill and old items are rarely read. Which table class?
back: DynamoDB Standard-IA, for lower storage costs.
extra: It is the most cost-effective class when storage is the dominant cost.

front: In DynamoDB, backups must survive a malicious delete by an administrator. What do you use?
back: AWS Backup Vault Lock, a write-once-read-many setting.
extra: AWS Backup can also copy backups to other accounts and Regions.

front: In a DynamoDB global table in the default mode, which write wins a conflict on one item?
back: The last writer wins.
extra: The default mode is multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC).

front: In DynamoDB, users may read only items whose partition key is their own ID. Which IAM condition key?
back: dynamodb:LeadingKeys, with the ForAllValues modifier.
extra: LeadingKeys is the first key attribute of the table: the partition key.

front: In DynamoDB, can one transaction write to tables in two Regions?
back: No. A transaction stays in one account and one Region.
extra: All tables of one transaction share one account and one Region.

front: In DynamoDB, can BatchWriteItem run UpdateItem requests?
back: No. BatchWriteItem does not support UpdateItem requests.
extra: Send each update as its own UpdateItem call.
